stories.text: From Media Jobs Report, this is your Morning Brief. A new study from WPP Media, System1 and TikTok finds creator ads work better when brands get to the point early. Mentioning the advertiser in the first two seconds — and using humor, storytelling or other entertaining elements — can significantly boost brand recognition and recall. The findings could also apply to podcast host reads and radio endorsements.

Riley Green is celebrating his new album, That’s Just Me, with an iHeartCountry Album Release Party Wednesday night. The special features a conversation with Green and a live performance, airing nationwide on iHeartCountry stations and streaming on YouTube starting at 7 p.m. Pacific.

Local Media Association says the Economic Opportunity Lab has released a free playbook for local newsrooms. The resource draws on a yearlong project involving 48 newsrooms and 10 NBC and Telemundo stations, offering a framework for using data to report on economic opportunity. For more information, log on to the Local Media Association website at local media dot org.

CNN is bringing Farm Aid back to television Saturday night. The four-hour live broadcast from Virginia Beach begins at 7 Eastern, featuring Willie Nelson, Neil Young, John Mellencamp, Dave Matthews, Margo Price and more. John Berman and Laura Coates will anchor CNN’s coverage.

The nominees are out for the 2026 Latin GRAMMY Awards. Karol G, Rosalía, Mon Laferte, Jorge Drexler and Milo J are among the artists represented in major categories including Record, Album and Song of the Year. The awards are set for November 12, with the complete nominee list available at Media Jobs Report.

Sinclair is expanding The National News Desk, adding a new 5 p.m. edition in 12 markets and daytime half-hour newscasts in 21 markets. The expansion began September 21 and brings additional national news programming to Sinclair stations throughout the afternoon and early evening. The National News Desk now airs on 90 stations nationwide.

NBCUniversal Local’s Clear The Shelters campaign helped more than 135,000 pets find new homes this year while raising nearly half a million dollars for animal shelters. More than 100 NBC and Telemundo stations participated. Since 2015, the campaign has helped nearly 1.5 million pets get adopted nationwide.

Early Bird registration is now open for Country Radio Seminar 2027. Save $100 for the two-day-only rate is $699 through September 23 before increasing to $799. CRS returns to Nashville March 17 through 19 with three days of education, networking, industry research and live entertainment. Register through Eventbrite

Broadcasters have less than a week to meet new FCC cybersecurity requirements. The commission has released an FAQ explaining the rules, including which equipment is covered, password requirements, security updates and remote access. Stations must comply with the new EAS cybersecurity rules by September 29. More details are available from the FCC.

The Alliance for Women in Media has named its 2026 Gracies Leadership Award honorees. TikTok’s Zenia Mucha will receive the inaugural Gracies Vanguard Award, while Kristen Welch receives the Legacy Leadership Award. Marilu Galvez, Tina Perry, Julie Talbott and Erin Underhill will also be honored November 16 in New York.

Comcast NBCUniversal and NBCUniversal Local are investing another $2.5 million in local communities. Eighty nonprofits across 11 NBC and Telemundo station markets are receiving unrestricted grants this year. Since 2018, the Local Impact Grants program has awarded more than $24 million to nearly 700 organizations nationwide.

New research shows podcast hosts may be one of the industry's most valuable assets. The Podcast Study 2026 found 82% of listeners with a favorite podcast say the host is a major reason they listen, while host-read endorsements also outperformed prerecorded ads in purchase influence.

CNN is promoting Leigh Waldman to correspondent. Beginning October 12, Waldman will be based in Los Angeles and report across CNN platforms. She moves up from CNN Newsource, where she covered major national stories for more than 1,000 affiliate partners. Before CNN, Waldman was an investigative reporter at KSAT in San Antonio.

Ella Langley is headed to Denver for an intimate SiriusXM Small Stage Series concert. She’ll perform Oct. 6 at The Grizzly Rose, with the full show airing Oct. 9 on SiriusXM’s The Highway. The performance comes as Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” sets a new Billboard Hot 100 record with 23 weeks at No. 1.

Hallmark Media has promoted Nick Barra to vice president of digital revenue operations. Barra has spent more than 13 years with the company, most recently as senior director of ad operations. He’ll now lead operational strategy and revenue functions supporting Hallmark’s growing digital advertising business across digital, connected TV and streaming platforms.

Paramount is lining up more financing for its Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. The company has launched syndication of a $7.5 billion term loan and says it plans to raise another $44.4 billion in secured debt. The money would help fund the WBD purchase and repay existing debt as Paramount works toward completing the massive media combination.

Taylor Swift has another big moment planned for Sunday’s MTV Video Music Awards. Her new “Patient Zero” music video, directed by Swift and starring Colin Farrell and Dakota Johnson, will make its world premiere during the show. The VMAs, hosted by Snoop Dogg, air Sunday night on CBS and MTV and stream on Paramount+.

Baltimore has a new sports radio station. WQLL-AM has launched FOX Sports 1370, carrying FOX Sports Radio’s weekday lineup including Dan Patrick, Colin Cowherd and Covino & Rich. The station has also added VSiN for nights and weekends, giving Baltimore sports talk and betting coverage throughout the week.

Podcast fans apparently aren’t choosing between audio and video — they’re using both. Acast’s Podcast Pulse 2026 found 78% of fans consume podcasts in multiple formats, and 63% have even started an episode one way and finished it another. The takeaway: where and when people listen may matter more than the format itself.

Philadelphia’s 92.5 XTU is going all Dolly on September 25. The station is celebrating Dolly Parton Day — with 9/25 serving as a nod to her hit “9 to 5.” XTU will feature Dolly’s music, stories and career highlights throughout the day, with listeners encouraged to add a little kindness and plenty of rhinestones.

TuneIn is headed into more connected cars. Stingray says a new global agreement with Stellantis will bring TuneIn directly into select future vehicles, giving drivers access to more than 100,000 radio stations, plus podcasts, music and news. The companies haven’t yet announced which Stellantis models will get the service.

Sony Music Group is becoming the first music company to join ARIAM, a global coalition promoting responsible artificial intelligence across creative industries. Sony says it will push for AI policies that protect artists and songwriters while supporting innovation, including licensing partnerships between AI companies and rights holders.

Houston Public Media is launching a $15.5 million Future Fund to strengthen its long-term financial future following the loss of federal funding. The campaign starts with $1 million from The Cullen Foundation and $100,000 from the Conely Foundation, with funding planned for local journalism, new audiences and additional revenue opportunities.

FOX Sports Radio is teaming Stugotz with Chris “The Bear” Fallica for a new college football podcast. “College Football with Stugotz & The Bear” debuts Friday and will drop new episodes Mondays and Fridays throughout the season, combining college football analysis, traditions and plenty of personality.

CMA is celebrating Dolly Parton with a live two-hour television tribute from Nashville on October 21. Tickets go on sale September 30 starting at $95, with proceeds supporting Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library. The special airs live on ABC and Disney+, with performers and guests still to be announced.

The New York Times Company is returning another quarterly dividend to shareholders. The company’s board declared a 23-cent-per-share dividend on both Class A and Class B stock. It’s payable October 22 to shareholders of record at the close of business October 7.

NBC is adding three new shows to its fall lineup. “The Traitors: New Blood” and the federal-agent family drama “Line of Fire” are already underway, while Téa Leoni and Tim Daly’s new comedy “Newlyweds” premieres October 23. All three air on NBC and stream the next day on Peacock.

Comcast has named longtime executive Thaddeus Lee senior vice president of its Texas Region. Lee, who has spent more than 20 years with the company, will oversee Xfinity and Comcast Business operations across southeast Texas, including growth, customer experience and network expansion. He most recently led sales and marketing for Comcast’s Beltway Region.

iHeartRadio has announced its 2026 Jingle Ball Tour, with Olivia Rodrigo, Jonas Brothers, Hilary Duff, OneRepublic and dozens more playing nine cities in December. The tour kicks off in Dallas-Fort Worth Dec. 1 and wraps in Nashville Dec. 17. Tickets go on sale to the public Oct. 2, with an ABC Jingle Ball special coming in December.

Media Jobs Report has added a new way to make your daily Prep more local — and maybe help an animal find a home. Adoptable Pets Near You highlights dogs and cats from rescue organizations around your area, with photos, adoption details and tools to share pets with your audience. Find it now at Media Jobs Report.

Cox Media Group has promoted Jud Heussler to Director of Operations for its eight-station Jacksonville Radio group. Heussler will oversee programming strategy and daily operations across the market. He joined CMG in 2021 and most recently led branding and programming for WAPE and WEZI. He succeeds Jules Riley, who moved to CMG Atlanta Radio this summer.

USA TODAY Co. and Lee Enterprises are reshuffling their newspaper portfolios. USA TODAY Co. is taking full control of the Arizona Daily Star, while Lee is acquiring the Sioux Falls Argus Leader, Aberdeen American News, Watertown Public Opinion and Great Falls Tribune. The agreements are effective immediately, with financial terms not disclosed.

Universal Music Group has named former Spotify executive Òscar Celma senior vice president of Applied AI and Machine Learning. Celma will help lead AI and machine-learning development across UMG’s global operations. His background also includes Condé Nast, Pandora/SiriusXM and Gracenote.

Beasley Media Group is the new official year-round audio partner of the Vegas Golden Knights. X 107.9 becomes the team’s English-language flagship, while 105.7 Maxima will carry Spanish-language broadcasts. The multiyear deal also includes expanded Golden Knights programming and coverage of the Henderson Silver Knights across Beasley’s audio platforms.

The E.W. Scripps Company has promoted Sean McGarvy to Head of News. Beginning October 5, McGarvy will lead news and content strategy while overseeing standards across Scripps’ local newsrooms, digital operations and national Scripps News network. The nearly 30-year news veteran most recently served as Senior Director of Digital News Operations.

The Society of Broadcast Engineers has named five recipients of its 2026 Ennes Educational Foundation Trust scholarships. Diovany Deus, Brendan Temkin, Adrianna Taliercio, Katie Herring and Tanner Denoyer will each receive three thousand dollars toward their education. The program supports students and professionals pursuing careers in broadcast engineering and media technology.

Audacy is bringing its We Can Survive concert to New York for the first time. Megan Moroney, Michelle Branch, Bebe Rexha and Ashe will perform Oct. 28 at UBS Arena. The 13th annual event benefits the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention and supports Audacy’s “I’m Listening” mental health initiative. Tickets go on sale Oct. 2.

A new identity is on the air in St. Louis. Sinclair has rebranded KDNL as STL30 as the former ABC affiliate moves forward as an independent station. The new STL30 branding is rolling out across the station’s on-air, digital and social platforms this week.

The U.S. job market remained relatively steady in August. New Labor Department data show 7.1 million job openings nationwide, with 5.2 million hires. For media-related employers, Information-sector openings jumped from 78,000 in July to 123,000 in August, although actual hiring in the sector declined.

Local Media Association is accepting applications for its new AI Growth Lab, developed in partnership with Google. Up to 12 local newsrooms will receive six months of AI training and coaching focused on audience growth, revenue and newsroom tools. Applications are due October 14.

Billy Bush is relaunching “Hot Mics” with a new look, new set and expanded live schedule. The show now streams live four days a week, covering entertainment, pop culture, news, politics and technology, with additional live editions planned when breaking stories warrant them. “Hot Mics with Billy Bush” is distributed by iHeartPodcasts.

The MTV Video Music Awards just posted their biggest audience in 11 years. The 2026 VMAs drew 8.43 million viewers across CBS and MTV, up 51% from last year. CBS alone averaged 7.61 million viewers, while the show also posted double-digit gains across key adult demographics.

Christian radio listeners want familiar favorites this Christmas. A new Finney Media study asked listeners nationwide to rank more than 200 holiday songs and found a preference for nostalgic, well-known versions of Christmas classics. The research is designed to help Christian stations plan their 2026 holiday programming.

Premiere Networks and Buzz Knight Media have launched “Jersey Made,” a new podcast hosted by veteran media executive Buzz Knight. The iHeartPodcasts series explores New Jersey’s musical legacy, with guests including Brian Williams and Brian Fallon and stories spanning Sinatra, Springsteen, Whitney Houston and more.

The final lineup is set for the 57th Annual GMA Dove Awards. Brandon Lake with Lainey Wilson, Tye Tribbett, Hope Darst and Elevation Worship are among the newly announced performers. Amy Grant and Natalie Grant will also share the stage for the first time for a special tribute to Dolly Parton. The Dove Awards take place Oct. 6 in Nashville and air Oct. 9 on TBN.

Compass Media Networks’ “She’s Country” has topped 40 affiliates just months after launching nationally. Hosted by Emily Harlan, the three-hour weekend show spotlights women in Country music with hits, emerging artists, interviews and behind-the-scenes stories. New affiliates include stations in Baton Rouge, Fresno, Tulsa, Traverse City and Medford.

Jacobs Media and the Public Media Content Collective will present Public Radio Techsurvey 2026 on Wednesday, October 7. The webinar will reveal new research from more than 17,000 Public Radio listeners, covering trust, fundraising, local content and changing digital habits. To register or for more information, visit Events at Media Jobs Report dot com.

The CMA Foundation is partnering with Lainey Wilson and Zach Top on $10,000 music education investments tied to their 2025 CMA Awards achievements, with Wilson also contributing an additional $5,000 through her Heart Like a Truck Fund.

Motown Gospel/TAMLA has promoted Justin Tomlinson to Vice President of Marketing. Tomlinson, previously Senior Director of Marketing, will lead marketing strategy for the label’s artists and releases. His career includes work with RCA Inspiration, Sony Music Nashville and Atlantic Records.

The Country Radio Hall of Fame is accepting nominations for its Class of 2027 through October 30. Eligible nominees must have at least 20 years in radio, including 15 in the country format. The new class will be announced during CRS 2027 in Nashville. Nominations can be submitted through the Country Radio Hall of Fame nomination form on the CRS website at Country Radio Seminar dot com.

The CW is adding NHRA drag racing to its growing sports lineup. Beginning in fall 2027, the network will carry the final seven races of the NHRA Mission Foods Drag Racing Series, including the U.S. Nationals and the complete six-race Countdown to the Championship playoffs.

Clay Travis and Buck Sexton are giving listeners a behind-the-scenes look at their Oval Office visit with President Donald Trump. The Premiere Networks hosts met with Trump on Monday and later shared details from the meeting, including encounters with several administration officials and plenty of conversation about college football.

Audiohook has acquired podcast intelligence platform Podscan and is opening much of its data to the industry for free. Podscan analyzes more than 70,000 podcast episodes daily for brand suitability, contextual categories, brand mentions and sentiment. Founder Arvid Kahl is joining Audiohook to oversee the platform’s technical transition and future development.

Radiocraft has selected Compass Media Networks to handle advertising sales for The TJ Show and LiveLine with Mason beginning January 1st. The TJ Show airs on more than 130 stations, while LiveLine with Mason is heard on more than 80 stations nationwide.

Hundreds of college radio stations around the world come together Friday for the 16th annual World College Radio Day. More than 40 countries now celebrate the event. Media Jobs Report supports future media professionals year-round with free internship search, scholarship search, airplay charts and real-world industry tools at MediaJobsReport.com.

California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed SB 690, changing the state’s Invasion of Privacy Act. The News/Media Alliance says the measure gives publishers greater protection from lawsuits involving commonly used website technologies while preserving California privacy protections.

Townsquare Media is expanding its digital advertising partnerships. The company has signed a deal with Lakes Media Network, giving its six radio brands in Virginia and North Carolina access to Townsquare Ignite’s programmatic advertising, audience targeting and performance reporting technology.

Nine PBS has been awarded more than $11 million in first-year federal Ready To Learn funding. The station will lead the new Everyday Literacy Alliance, expand Teaching in Room 9 nationally, and partner with Fred Rogers Productions on a new preschool literacy program called Fredosaurus Rex.

Universal Music Group is expanding Frank Briegmann’s international leadership role. Briegmann has been promoted to Chairman and CEO of Universal Music Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Deutsche Grammophon. UMG says the new structure is designed to increase collaboration across markets and create more opportunities for local artists to reach audiences worldwide. Briegmann joined Universal Music in 2004 and will continue reporting to Chairman and CEO Sir Lucian Grainge.

TikTok supported an estimated $81 billion in U.S. GDP and 410,000 American jobs in 2025, according to a new PF Global report. The study also found TikTok discovery generated $4.7 billion in local spending, while 93% of businesses surveyed reported increased sales after promoting on the platform.

From Miami, iHeartMedia is kicking off its 2026 Fiesta Latina celebration with a free party at the Miami Design District on October 15. Enrique Santos and Dayanara Torres will host the event, featuring Tony Succar’s Unity: The Latin Tribute to Michael Jackson, along with Jean Rodriguez, Anthony Ramos and Backstreet Boys member Howie D. The celebration leads into the main iHeartRadio Fiesta Latina concert on October 17 at Kaseya Center, featuring Anuel AA, Myke Towers, Farruko, Manuel Turizo and more. Lin-Manuel Miranda will also receive the 2026 iHeartRadio Corazón Latino Award.

Sounds Profitable’s Podcast Landscape 2026 finds podcast reach holding steady, with 74% of U.S. adults having consumed a podcast. Video continues to grow, while Netflix has emerged as the third most-named podcast platform behind YouTube and Spotify.

Nielsen will roll out new cross-platform content measurement solutions in early 2027. The system will combine publishers’ first-party streaming data with Nielsen panels and big data to measure total reach and time spent across screens. An AI-assisted interface is also planned, with the technology eventually contributing to reports including The Gauge.
Media Jobs Report has launched new airplay charts featuring station spin counts from 2,971 monitored U.S. stations. View the charts now at Media Jobs Report dot com.

New Pew-Knight Initiative research finds Americans broadly value press freedom but differ on its limits. About half say news organizations are greatly influenced by corporate or political interests, while many support some restrictions involving false information or national security. The findings come from Pew Research Center surveys of U.S. adults.

The lineup is set for the 57th Annual GMA Dove Awards Pre-Telecast Show. Sarai Rivera and CalledOut Music will host and perform, with Chelsea Plank, Lloyd Nicks and The Grascals also taking the stage. The Pre-Telecast happens Tuesday, October 6, in Nashville, with an online broadcast October 10.

Warner Music Mexico has promoted Yusim Aladro to General Manager. The veteran music executive will oversee strategy and development for the company’s domestic roster, bringing together A&R, creative marketing and artist brand building to help expand the global reach of Mexican artists.

Veteran higher education journalist Doug Lederman has joined the Board of Directors of Open Campus. Lederman co-founded Inside Higher Ed in 2004 and served as its editor until 2024. Before launching Inside Higher Ed, he held several positions at The Chronicle of Higher Education and began his journalism career as a news clerk at The New York Times. Open Campus Co-Founder and CEO Scott Smallwood says Lederman brings extensive experience at the intersection of journalism and higher education.

Nielsen will roll out new cross-platform content measurement solutions in early 2027. The system will combine publishers’ first-party streaming data with Nielsen panels and big data to measure total reach and time spent across screens. An AI-assisted interface is also planned, with the technology eventually contributing to reports including The Gauge.

NRB has welcomed 11 new members for the third quarter of 2026, including Christian media, radio, publishing, ministry and communications organizations and professionals. New members include Prayz Network, Cornerstone Chapel, Advantage Books, Jonah Wiley and Chris Free. NRB also welcomed back Wild Brothers Productions and North Greenville University.

Anthony Anderson will host the 2026 Soul Train Awards as the celebration returns to Chicago. The show airs Friday, November 27 at 8 p.m. ET/PT on BET and CBS, with performers and honorees to be announced.

The National Association of Broadcasters is accepting entries for the 41st annual Crystal Radio Awards. NAB member radio stations have until October 31 to submit their community service efforts. Fifty finalists will be announced in February, with 10 winners honored in Washington in March.

Skydance has unveiled the 17-member leadership team expected to run the company following completion of Paramount's Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. David Ellison will serve as Chairman and CEO, with Ynon Kreiz as Co-CEO. The team includes senior leaders overseeing corporate operations, film, television, streaming, DC Studios, CNN and CBS News. Read full story at Media Jobs Report dot com.

Hubbard Seattle has launched Bull Classics, airing on KKNW-AM 1150 and 98.9 HD2. The Classic Country format features George Strait, Reba McEntire, Garth Brooks and other country favorites. It complements 98.9 The Bull’s New Country programming.

BET has announced the 2026 Soul Train Awards nominees, and fans will vote for the first time in two new categories: R&B/Soul Song of the Year and Spotify’s RNB X International Artist. Voting is open through October 16, with the awards airing November 27 on BET and CBS.

Nexstar and DAZN are teaming up to make 15 Indiana Pacers games available free this season. The games will air on Nexstar stations in Indianapolis, Evansville and Champaign and stream free on DAZN, beginning October 23 against Dallas.

The Society of Broadcast Engineers has named Andrew Sveum its new Marketing and Growth Director. The newly created position is part of SBE’s strategic plan to expand its reach, strengthen member engagement and support long-term organizational growth.

Tickets for the 62nd Academy of Country Music Awards go on sale to the public October 9 at 10 a.m. Pacific. The awards return to Las Vegas on May 16, 2027, with presales for American Express members and ACM A-List subscribers beginning October 6 and 7. Find ticket details at AXS.com.

MIW and the NAB Leadership Foundation are accepting applications for the 2026 LAUNCH Mentorship Program through October 30. Sponsored by Mr. Master, the program now includes women working for broadcast technology partners and vendors, with the selected mentee also attending the 2027 NAB Show in Las Vegas. More information and links to apply are available on Media Jobs Report.

The Local Media Association has released a new AI roadmap for local broadcasters. Developed with support from the Google News Initiative, the report examines how AI can streamline content production, sales, video distribution and archive searches while keeping journalists and human editorial oversight at the center. More information is available at Media Jobs Report dot com.

The National Association of Broadcasters has made two leadership appointments to its Radio Board. Townsquare Media Chief Operating Officer Erik Hellum has been named first vice chair of the Radio Board executive committee. Salem Media Group CEO Dave Santrella has also been appointed to the NAB Radio Board, representing the New England District. Both appointments are effective immediately.

CMA has announced five promotions across the organization. Michelle Kirk will lead the CMA Foundation as Executive Director, while Sydnie Hickey moves up to Director of Lifecycle Marketing and Reuben Schwartz becomes Director of Business Intelligence. Ansley Carlson and Katie Karl also received promotions as CMA strengthens several key departments.

Gracie Abrams is heading to New York City for an exclusive SiriusXM Small Stage Series concert at Irving Plaza on October 24. She’ll perform songs from her new album, Daughter from Hell, along with fan favorites. SiriusXM Hits 1 will begin airing the performance October 30, with additional songs featured across several SiriusXM channels.

800 Pound Gorilla has named Russell Weissman Head of Licensing. The former All Things Comedy Chief Operating Officer brings more than 15 years of media experience and will help expand licensing, distribution and partnerships as the Nashville-based comedy company continues its growth.

Skydance is adding some major names to its Board. Laurene Powell Jobs, former Activision CEO Bobby Kotick and Ynon Kreiz are joining as directors, while former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair will serve as an advisor. David Ellison remains Chairman and CEO as Skydance brings Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery together.

Saga Communications has promoted John Hakim to General Manager of Charleston Media Solutions. Hakim spent the past five years as Director of Sales and succeeds Paul O’Malley, who recently moved into Saga’s Senior Vice President of Revenue Development role. Hakim previously worked for Cox Media Group in Jacksonville.

USA TODAY Sports and PlayVS are launching a National High School Esports Championship. Eight teams will compete in Madden NFL, Marvel Rivals and Rocket League beginning October 12, with the top two advancing to the championship December 11. The tournament will also produce an inaugural ALL-USA Esports Team.

The CMA is bringing together some of country music’s biggest stars for a live celebration of Dolly Parton. Carrie Underwood, Reba McEntire, Lainey Wilson, Brad Paisley and more will perform Oct. 21 on ABC and Disney+. Proceeds will benefit Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library.

Podtrac's September rankings are out. Crime Junkie remains America's top podcast, followed by The Daily, NPR News Now, Up First and Dateline NBC. iHeart Audience Network leads both the U.S. publisher ranking and Podtrac's global multi-channel podcast ranking.

Lauren Alaina brought her new album Stages to Live With Kelly and Mark, performing “Never Been In Love.” The appearance comes as her Chase Matthew collaboration “All My Exes” enters the Top 5 at country radio. Alaina is currently headlining The Stages Tour, including a November 12 Ryman Auditorium debut.

Hubbard South Florida gave 20 students a behind-the-scenes look at radio broadcasting. The Home School Palm Beach dot com group toured the studios and met personalities from New Country 103.1 and X102.3 while learning how shows are produced and exploring potential careers in media.

Dick Clark’s New Year’s Rockin’ Eve is expanding to streaming. The 2027 celebration will air live on both ABC and Disney+ for the first time. Ryan Seacrest returns as host, with Druski in Chicago, Rita Ora in Times Square, and Julianne Hough and Rob Gronkowski in Las Vegas.

Audacy has a new morning team at New York's legendary WCBS-FM. Veteran broadcasters Trey Morgan and Loren Raye will host weekdays from six to ten. Morgan brings experience from major markets nationwide, while Raye is a two-time Gracie Award winner. The pair will lead mornings on one of America's top Classic Hits stations.

The Alliance for Women in Media Foundation has opened entries for the 52nd Annual Gracie Awards. Eligible television, radio, streaming, podcast and digital work from 2026 can compete, with an early-bird deadline of December 10. National winners will be honored next May in Beverly Hills.

NBCUniversal is accepting applications for its Spring 2027 Page Program through October 19. The paid program gives early-career professionals three rotational assignments across NBCUniversal businesses in New York or Universal City, California. The new class begins January 25. Candidates can submit an application through the NBCUniversal Careers Page Program site.

Gray Media is expanding free local access to Minnesota Timberwolves basketball. Stations in four Minnesota and Wisconsin markets will simulcast 15 games this season under a new agreement with TEGNA and DAZN, with select games also airing on Gray’s major network affiliates.

Two stars of A Different World are getting back together! Kadeem Hardison and Darryl M. Bell are launching A Different World View, a new weekly podcast from iHeartMedia's Black Effect Podcast Network. The show premieres October 15, with Debbie Allen as the first guest. Expect behind-the-scenes stories, laughs and plenty of nostalgia.

Zixi has named John Towers its new Chief Financial Officer. Towers brings more than 20 years of experience, including leadership positions at Sony, Deluxe and Fabric Data. He'll oversee financial operations as Zixi expands its technology for broadcasters and streaming companies moving from traditional satellite distribution to IP-based video delivery.

Boston-based GBH is welcoming three new trustees as it celebrates its 75th anniversary. Ingrid Chung of Fidelity Investments, Jonathan Goldstein of TA Associates, and John Kennedy of UMass Amherst join the board, bringing experience in finance, education and journalism. The appointments come as GBH continues expanding its public media services.

The Academy is now accepting media credential applications for the 99th Oscars, happening March 14, 2027. News organizations can apply for in-person or virtual backstage Interview Room access. Applications must be submitted by November 23 at 5 p.m. Pacific. Visit press dot oscars dot org for details.

Five major media companies have scheduled their third-quarter earnings announcements. SiriusXM reports October 29, followed by Sinclair on November 4. Nexstar and Scripps release results November 5, while Charter reports November 6. The announcements will provide a fresh look at financial performance across broadcasting, audio and broadband.

Spotify and Joe Rogan are staying together. The streaming company has announced a new multi-year licensing agreement for The Joe Rogan Experience, which has 18 million Spotify followers. New episodes will continue appearing on Spotify and other platforms. Financial terms were not disclosed. Rogan says he's excited to continue the partnership for years to come.

The Encouragers' Radio Rally podcast has released a free fourth-quarter radio sales event. Host Loyd Ford joins Chris Fleming, Josh Brown and Big John Small to share practical ideas for increasing local advertising revenue, strengthening client relationships and creating new business opportunities. The complete discussion is available now on SoundCloud.

Scripps News is bringing back Connected with Alisyn Camerota October 13, with Harry Connick Jr. opening the seven-episode season. The network is also launching new episodes of The Originals, Caught on Clips and In the Shadows, alongside expanded midterm election coverage.

Alex Warren will host the 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards on November 14, airing live on CBS and Nickelodeon. Taylor Swift leads with six nominations, followed by Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter with five each. Fans can vote in 36 categories at Kids Choice Awards dot com.

The New York Times has named Renée Rippberger an Editorial Assistant in its Opinion department, supporting columnist Thomas Friedman. Rippberger previously worked at the Brookings Institution on democracy and rule of law projects. She brings international research experience from Armenia and Europe and will work from the newspaper’s Washington bureau.

Tuesday, October 13th is International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction, encouraging awareness of natural disasters and the importance of emergency preparedness. Media Jobs Report has released 12 free, one-page emergency preparedness guides covering hurricanes, tornadoes, floods, wildfires, earthquakes, power outages and more. Each guide includes practical safety tips, emergency supply recommendations and links to trusted government resources. The guides are free to download, print and share, with no registration required. Get all 12 guides at Media Jobs Report dot com

FEMA is hosting two free webinars to help broadcasters prepare for the November 17th National Emergency Alert System test. The sessions are scheduled for October 16th at 11 a.m. Eastern and October 20th at 2:30 p.m. Eastern. Both webinars will cover test procedures and preparation tips. More information is available including links to register at Media Jobs Report dot com.

In Philadelphia, KYW Newsradio has inducted longtime radio executive David Yadgaroff into its Hall of Fame. Yadgaroff joined the station in 1992 and rose through the ranks to become Audacy Philadelphia's Senior Vice President and Market Manager. He retired in May after a 36-year radio career. The honor recognizes his leadership, mentorship and lasting contributions to Philadelphia broadcasting.

TEGNA CEO Patrick Paolini has named Joan Barrett, Kate Morris and Brad Ramsey group general managers, completing the company’s new leadership team. Each will oversee stations in two regions, supporting local managers with strategy, business performance and audience growth. Barrett will lead the Northeast and Southeast, Morris the Midwest and West, and Ramsey Texas and the Mid-South.

Compass Media Networks has secured exclusive national audio rights to the Pac-12 football championship and men's and women's basketball championship games through a multi-year agreement with the conference and Playfly Sports. Coverage begins December fourth, with broadcasts available on radio, streaming and satellite platforms. The basketball championships follow in March.

Investigative Reporters and Editors has received a twenty-five-thousand-dollar legacy gift from its late executive director, Diana Fuentes, who passed away earlier this year. The organization will use the donation to support staff and journalism training. IRE is also establishing a workshop in her honor, with the first session planned for 2027.

In Philadelphia, Comcast is teaming up with WMMR’s Preston and Steve Show for its annual Camp Out for Hunger food drive. Through November thirteenth, 31 participating Xfinity Stores across Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Delaware are collecting non-perishable food donations for Philabundance. Comcast will deliver the donations to Camp Out for Hunger on November twentieth.

The Country Music Association has announced its 2026 Broadcast Awards winners, with Country star Zach Top personally calling the honorees. For National Personality of the Year, Buzz Brainard's Highway Hot 30 Countdown won the weekly category, while Big D and Bubba took daily honors. In local personality awards, The Andie Summers Show on WXTU Philadelphia won Major Market. The Jesse and Anna Show on WUBE Cincinnati took Large Market. Steve and Gina on KXKT Omaha won Medium Market, and Officer Don and DeAnn on WBUL Lexington earned Small Market honors. Station of the Year winners include KSCS Dallas for Major Market, WQDR Raleigh for Large Market, KXKT Omaha for Medium Market, and WKML Fayetteville for Small Market. All winners will be recognized November 18th during the 60th Annual CMA Awards in Nashville.

Northwestern University's latest Medill report finds local news deserts are growing at their fastest pace in five years. Twenty-six additional U.S. counties lost their last locally based news source, bringing the total to 238. Newspaper closures now average three per week, while employment continues to decline. Researchers also found that ten broadcasting groups control three-quarters of local TV newsrooms.

TEGNA and Disney Entertainment Television have renewed ABC affiliation agreements for 13 TEGNA stations in a multi-year deal. The stations include WFAA in Dallas, KVUE in Austin and WZZM in Grand Rapids. TEGNA says the agreement extends its long-standing partnership with Disney

Cumulus Media has promoted Kathy “KB” Brown to Vice President of Urban Formats. Brown will oversee programming for 40 stations nationwide across Urban Mainstream, Urban AC, Classic Hip Hop and Gospel formats. She'll also continue as Program Director and On-Air Talent for Z93 JAMZ and Magic 107.3 in Charleston, South Carolina. Brown joined Cumulus in 2017 and brings extensive major-market programming experience to the position.

The 2026 International Women’s Podcast Awards honored outstanding audio storytelling during a ceremony in Toronto. Freedom Needs a Soundtrack earned two awards for visionary leadership and insight from a role model. Other winners included Debt Heads for comedy, Everybody Knows But Me for storytelling, Points North for behind-the-scenes brilliance, and Two-Faced: John of God for pure emotion. Well Beyond Medicine received the award for Changing the World One Moment at a Time.

The New York Times has won two Gerald Loeb Awards for excellence in business and financial journalism. The newspaper earned top honors for investigative reporting examining financial benefits tied to President Trump and for breaking news coverage of his Liberation Day tariffs. Times journalists were also finalists in seven additional categories, including international reporting, personal finance and visual storytelling. The awards recognize outstanding business and economic journalism.

The Radio Hall of Fame has welcomed eight new members. The Class of 2026 includes Boomer Esiason, Dennis Green, Shotgun Tom Kelly, Helen Little, Bob Pittman, Rickey Smiley, Charlie Van Dyke and Fred Winston. Bobby Bones hosted the induction ceremony October eighth in Chicago, celebrating the broadcasters and executives who helped shape radio.

The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has named Tatti Ribeiro and Noora Niasari recipients of its 2026 Gold Fellowship for Women, presented with CHANEL. Ribeiro earned recognition for her debut film, Valentina, while Niasari directed the award-winning Shayda. The yearlong fellowship provides mentorship, networking and career development opportunities for emerging women filmmakers.

Global advertising spending is expected to jump nearly 12 percent to $1.34 trillion this year, according to WARC Media. Social media leads the growth, with spending up more than 21 percent, while search and retail media also post double-digit gains. WARC expects the worldwide advertising market to reach $1.57 trillion by 2028, fueled by digital platforms and artificial intelligence.

iHeartMedia has revealed the lineup for its 2027 ALTer EGO concert, happening January 16th at the Kia Forum in Los Angeles. The show features Evanescence, The Offspring, Billy Corgan, Death Cab for Cutie, Slightly Stoopid, Modest Mouse, Young the Giant, The Warning, and Temper City. Woody from ALT 98.7's nationally syndicated Woody Show will host. The concert will air live on iHeartRadio Alternative and Rock stations nationwide and through the iHeartRadio app. Tickets go on sale to the general public October 23rd, with earlier presales for eligible Capital One cardholders and ALT 98.7 VIP members.

M-I-W is accepting applications for its third annual Digital Sales Mentorship Program. One woman working in radio or digital media sales will receive a year of personalized coaching, covering digital marketing, streaming, podcasting, revenue strategies and leadership development. Applicants must have at least three years of sales experience. The deadline is November sixth. Details are available at Radio M-I-W dot com.

Cumulus Media’s NewsTalk 580 and 105.9 K-M-J in Fresno has raised a record 428 thousand dollars for the Central California Food Bank. The station partnered with Gar Incorporated for its 13th annual Feeding Families Fund Drive. The one-day event will provide more than 1.7 million meals to families in need. Over 13 years, the campaign has raised more than 5.5 million dollars.

Warner Records Group has named longtime music executive Jim Roppo Vice Chairman. Roppo joins after nearly three decades at Universal Music Group, most recently serving as Chairman and CEO of Republic Records. Based in Los Angeles, he'll oversee operations across Warner's labels and report to Chairman and CEO Aaron Bay-Schuck. His start date has not been announced.

Meta AI's Bridget Bogee says the future of artificial intelligence will move beyond chatbots toward personalized digital assistants that manage work and everyday responsibilities. Speaking during the Alliance for Women in Media's October Office Hours, Bogee emphasized that human creativity and judgment remain essential. Her career advice? “Go where you’re wanted,” encouraging professionals to seek leaders who recognize their talents.

In Indianapolis, 99.5 ZPL's Smiley Morning Show is celebrating its 24th annual Pumpkin Drop Today at the Indiana State Fairgrounds. The free family event features a nearly fourteen-hundred-pound pumpkin crashing from hundreds of feet above the ground, plus trick-or-treating, games and entertainment. The big splat happens around eight Thursday morning.

Country Radio Broadcasters is accepting applications for the Rusty Walker Scholarship, giving one first-time attendee a chance to attend Country Radio Seminar 2027 in Nashville. The scholarship covers registration, round-trip airfare, and hotel accommodations. Applicants must be full-time radio station employees who have never attended CRS. The application deadline is November 12. Details are available at Country Radio Seminar dot com.

The Local Media Association and Northwestern University's Medill Local News Initiative have released a new fundraising playbook for local newsrooms. The report shares strategies and case studies from a three-month program involving nine Midwestern news organizations. Topics include donor management, fundraising events and philanthropic support. The free report is available through the Local Media Association.

TEGNA has announced four senior sales leadership appointments. Jay Donovan becomes vice president of digital sales, while Kristie Gonzales will oversee Northeast and Southeast advertising sales. Kari Jacobs takes responsibility for the Midwest and West, and Byron Wilkinson will lead Texas and Mid-South sales. The appointments are part of TEGNA's strategy to strengthen regional revenue and expand digital advertising growth.

Triton Digital is expanding its audio advertising capabilities through a new partnership with Datonics. The integration gives radio stations, podcasters, and digital audio publishers access to more precise audience targeting based on demographics, consumer behavior, and purchasing interests. Available in 12 countries, the technology is designed to help advertisers reach the right listeners while creating new revenue opportunities for audio publishers.

iHeartMedia has announced the celebrity presenters for Saturday's iHeartRadio Fiesta Latina in Miami. The lineup includes Lele Pons, Howie D of the Backstreet Boys, and several other personalities. Anuel AA, Myke Towers, and Farruko are among the scheduled performers, while Lin-Manuel Miranda will receive the Corazón Latino Award. The concert will air nationwide on iHeartRadio's Latin stations and app.

TelevisaUnivision has named Elizabeth “Liz” Roldán Vice President of News for WLTV 23 N+ Univision Miami. Roldán returns to the station where she began her television career as an intern. Her experience includes newsroom leadership at WFOR and WTVJ in Miami, along with KHOU and KIAH in Houston. The award-winning journalist will oversee editorial operations, content strategy and multiplatform news coverage serving South Florida's Hispanic community.

Investigative Reporters and Editors has unanimously approved a revised Code of Conduct aimed at strengthening safety, inclusion and accountability. The updated policy now covers all IRE activities, not just events, and establishes clearer rules for reporting complaints, investigating violations and handling appeals. IRE says the changes take effect immediately and apply to members, staff, speakers and other participants.

Skydance is bringing back The Concert for New York City to mark its 25th anniversary. Originally staged just weeks after September 11th, the historic benefit featured Paul McCartney, Billy Joel, David Bowie and more. MTV, VH1, MTV2 and Logo will rebroadcast the concert Tuesday, October 20th, beginning at 7 p.m. Eastern, supporting New York anti-poverty organization Robin Hood.

Audacy is partnering with viral creator Melani Sanders to launch "The We Do Not Care Club Podcast" on October twenty-first. The thirteen-episode series will explore menopause, wellness, relationships and midlife, featuring guests including Bobbi Brown and Ricki Lake. Audacy will handle advertising sales and distribution, with new episodes released weekly.

CNN has announced a multi-year partnership with Google to explore how generative artificial intelligence can help audiences discover and engage with its journalism. The agreement gives Google enhanced content rights for experimental AI features while compensating CNN for the use of its reporting. The network says the partnership supports its broader strategy of embracing AI while protecting its intellectual property.

Cumulus Media has emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy after eliminating 550 million dollars in debt. The restructuring gives the company a stronger financial position as it transitions to private ownership. CEO Mary Berner will continue leading Cumulus, which operates 377 radio stations across 84 markets, along with Westwood One and the Cumulus Podcast Network.

TEGNA has named Tim Thomas to lead its Atlanta television stations, WXIA and WATL, along with WMAZ in Macon, Georgia. Thomas moves from overseeing TEGNA’s Tampa and Jacksonville operations and brings more than 20 years of broadcast leadership experience. He succeeds Kristie Gonzales, who has been promoted to a regional advertising sales leadership role. Thomas previously worked at WXIA and says he’s excited to return to Atlanta.

The National Association of Broadcasters is preparing for a major leadership change. Rick Kaplan, NAB’s chief legal officer, will depart at the end of 2026 after more than 14 years. Kaplan helped secure major victories involving broadcast ownership rules, streaming royalties, and regulatory fees. Beginning January first, Shawn Donilon will become chief advocacy officer, overseeing NAB’s combined Government Relations and Legal teams.

Cumulus Media has emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy after eliminating 550 million dollars in debt. The restructuring gives the company a stronger financial position as it transitions to private ownership. CEO Mary Berner will continue leading Cumulus, which operates 377 radio stations across 84 markets, along with Westwood One and the Cumulus Podcast Network.
