Kaplan helped secure major victories involving broadcast ownership rules, streaming royalties, and regulatory fees. Beginning January first, Shawn Donilon will become chief advocacy officer, overseeing NAB’s combined Government Relations and Legal teams.

TEGNA has named Tim Thomas to lead its Atlanta television stations, WXIA and WATL, along with WMAZ in Macon, Georgia. Thomas moves from overseeing TEGNA’s Tampa and Jacksonville operations and brings more than 20 years of broadcast leadership experience. He succeeds Kristie Gonzales, who has been promoted to a regional advertising sales leadership role. Thomas previously worked at WXIA and says he’s excited to return to Atlanta.

Connoisseur Media’s 103.1 The Wolf on Long Island is adding a new twist to country radio weekends. New York DJ and producer Deerock joins the station with Club Rodeo Country Takeover, mixing country hits with electronic dance beats. Deerock has generated more than 232 million career streams and performed at major events including Stagecoach and EDC Las Vegas. The show airs Fridays at five and Saturdays at midnight.

Gray Media is partnering with Hoda Kotb's wellness company, Joy 101, to bring weekly health segments to local newscasts and the syndicated program Aging Untold beginning in January. The features will include journalist Karen Swensen and cardiologist Dr. Stephanie Moore. Kotb will also make guest appearances on Aging Untold, which reaches nearly 40 percent of U.S. television households.

As radio stations prepare for Christmas, Brian Wright of Wright Media Group has released a Comprehensive Christmas Programming Guide. The guide features creative listener promotions, community outreach ideas, holiday programming specials, and opportunities to generate sponsor revenue. Wright encourages stations to focus on memorable experiences that build stronger connections with listeners. Review the complete guide at Media Jobs Report dot com.

Apple Podcasts says video is delivering major audience gains for leading shows. In a new PodBiz interview, executive Jake Shapiro revealed that top podcasts adding video saw audiences grow more than 20 percent, while new followers jumped over 130 percent. Apple's HLS technology also creates new opportunities for advertising across audio and video.

The 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards take over Miami Thursday, October 22, with 16 musical performances airing live on Telemundo and Peacock. Wisin, Ivy Queen, Ozuna and Manuel Turizo are among the performers. The ceremony will also honor Rosalía, Rubén Blades, Cristian Castro and Fuerza Regida, while introducing its first-ever fan-voted award. The broadcast begins at 8 p.m. Eastern.

Jon Stewart is staying with Comedy Central's The Daily Show through December 2028. Stewart will continue hosting Mondays and serving as executive producer, while the show's news team handles Tuesday through Thursday. The extension follows two Emmy wins and strong ratings growth, with The Daily Show generating 1.9 billion social media views this year.

Audacy has launched US 96.5, Philadelphia's newest country radio station, featuring artists like Morgan Wallen, Luke Combs and Jelly Roll. The station is commercial-free through October 24, with its weekday lineup beginning October 26. A new morning show will be announced soon. US 96.5 becomes Audacy's 24th country station nationwide.

Rob Wagman will lead Manna, SonicTrek Media’s new localized Contemporary Christian radio format. The service will pair market-specific music and content with radio personalities, including longtime host Sparkle. Wagman previously worked with KFSH in Los Angeles and WAY-FM.

Fox Corporation is making changes to its legal leadership. Chief Legal and Policy Officer Adam Ciongoli will step down December first, transitioning to a special advisor role through June 2028. Nicholas Trutanich, currently Principal Deputy General Counsel, will become General Counsel, reporting directly to CEO Lachlan Murdoch. Trutanich joined FOX in 2021 and previously served as U.S. Attorney for Nevada. The company is also adjusting its government relations reporting structure.

Audacy is bringing The Bret Mega Show to Atlanta mornings on Star 94.1. Hosted by Bret Mega and Anna Bohlmann, the program airs weekdays from six to ten Eastern. The personality-driven show also airs in Kansas City, St. Louis and Wichita, expanding its reach across four Audacy markets.

Telemundo Las Vegas has named Alejandro Sánchez a multimedia journalist for its local newscasts. Sánchez joins KBLR from Telemundo 40 in the Rio Grande Valley, where he covered immigration and border communities. His background also includes international reporting and production work for TelevisaUnivision. He began his new role Monday.

The Academy of Country Music Awards will return to Las Vegas on May sixteenth, twenty twenty-seven, with tickets now on sale. The sixty-second annual ceremony will stream worldwide on Prime Video from the MGM Grand Garden Arena. Last year's event generated an estimated fifty-three million dollars for the Las Vegas economy, while attracting more than one hundred fifty-three million social media video views.

FEMA is preparing broadcasters for the nationwide Emergency Alert System test scheduled for November 17 at 2:20 p.m. Eastern.

The one-minute test will reach radio and television stations through FEMA's internet-based alert system, with traditional broadcast monitoring providing backup. Stations should verify equipment connectivity, audio quality, and automatic retransmission settings before test day. Broadcasters must also submit their FCC EAS reporting Form One by October 30.

CBS has revealed the first performers for its New Year's Eve Live: Nashville's Big Bash. HARDY, Little Big Town and ACM Award-winning group The Red Clay Strays will take the stage for the nearly five-hour celebration on December 31. The special airs on CBS and streams on Paramount Plus, with additional performers to be announced. Fans can also attend the free downtown Nashville celebration featuring the traditional midnight Music Note Drop.

Cumulus Media has launched a new local morning show on Indianapolis station 107.9 The Mix. The Morning Mix with Toni and Ryan pairs Toni DeKeyser and Ryan Swiger weekdays from six to ten. The launch also reshuffles midday programming between The Mix and sister station 99.5 ZPL, while Swiger continues afternoon drive on ZPL.

Investigative Reporters and Editors has named three journalists to its 2027 Chauncey Bailey Fellowship. Daisy Zavala Magaña, Miguel Torres and Nushrat Rahman will investigate farmworker pesticide exposure, immigration-service fraud and rental housing conditions. The yearlong program provides training and mentorship while honoring the legacy of Oakland investigative journalist Chauncey Bailey.

nextKast has released version 7.1.4 of its radio automation software, adding new tools to improve commercial scheduling and station operations. The update introduces nextTraffic Audit, allowing broadcasters to verify that all advertising spots are scheduled and quickly correct incomplete logs. Other improvements include enhanced traffic scheduling, format monitoring and fixes for live playout operations. The update is available now from nextKast.

Gordon Deal’s This Morning, America’s First News is expanding its reach, adding 20 new affiliates, including KMOX in St. Louis, WCCO in Minneapolis, and KMBX in Las Vegas. The Compass Media Networks program now airs on more than 325 stations, reaching 91 of the nation’s top 100 radio markets. Deal says the growth is both humbling and motivating.

The University of Washington has opened a new four-control-room broadcast production facility powered by Grass Valley technology. Called Sundodger Studios, the IP-based center can handle multiple live sporting events simultaneously, while giving students hands-on experience with professional cameras, production switchers and broadcast workflows.

The New York Times is accepting applications for its 2027-28 journalism fellowship. The paid, yearlong program offers early-career journalists opportunities in reporting, video, visuals, data journalism and audience engagement. Applicants must have fewer than five years of professional journalism experience. The fellowship begins June seventh, 2027, and applications close November twentieth.

KROQ in Los Angeles has announced the lineup for its 35th Almost Acoustic Christmas concert, December 12 at the Kia Forum. Foo Fighters, Weezer, Sublime and Interpol headline the event, alongside four additional acts. Tickets go on sale October 30, with proceeds benefiting two Los Angeles youth organizations.

The National Association of Broadcasters has announced its 2026 Marconi Radio Award winners. WBMX in Boston earned Major Market Station of the Year, while Karson and Kennedy won Major Market Personality honors. WIVK in Knoxville was named Legendary Station of the Year, and Julie Koehn of WLEN in Michigan received Legendary Radio Manager of the Year. Houston stations collected three format awards, and Joel Oxley of Hubbard Radio Washington received the NAB National Radio Award for his industry leadership. Read the story and review the complete list of winners at Media Jobs Report dot com.

A new national podcast study reveals opportunities to increase revenue without adding more commercials. The Podcast Study 2026 found that nearly 55 percent of listeners believe podcasts already carry too many ads. However, 40 percent say host-read endorsements strongly influence purchasing decisions. Researchers also found strong interest in free VIP clubs, premium content, and memberships priced below five dollars monthly. And social media is three times more effective at podcast discovery than advertising within other podcasts. The study surveyed more than 1,200 U.S. podcast consumers and was conducted by Strategic Solutions Research and Point-To-Point Marketing.

NBC Universal Media Group Chairman Matt Strauss says live sports, artificial intelligence, and new streaming partnerships are shaping Peacock's future. Speaking at the In the Arena conference, Strauss said Peacock is evolving beyond a streaming service into a broader entertainment platform. NBC Universal reports 225 million Americans watched its major February sports programming, including the Super Bowl and Winter Olympics. The company is also expanding its partnership with YouTube, with a Peacock Premium bundle planned for 2027. Strauss says artificial intelligence and personalized viewing experiences will help drive future audience growth.

Audacy's NEW 102.7 raised more than sixteen thousand dollars for VEG Cares during its third annual Anthony's Walk for Animals. Morning show co-host Anthony "Intern Ant" Malerba walked nearly fourteen miles across Staten Island, encouraging listeners to donate. The event also featured support from the Staten Island Tech High School Marching Band. Proceeds help provide emergency veterinary care for pets whose families cannot afford lifesaving treatment.

Entravision Communications has appointed former Intel CEO Brian Krzanich and financial executive Gary Ferrera to its Board of Directors. Krzanich brings decades of technology and artificial intelligence experience, while Ferrera has more than 30 years of financial leadership experience. Entravision says the appointments will help accelerate growth in its advertising technology business. Longtime directors Fehmi Zeko and Gilbert Vasquez are also preparing to leave the board.

Premiere Networks is bringing country music's biggest stars together for Thanksgiving with the annual *After MidNite Friendsgiving Special*, hosted by Granger Smith. The four-hour program features Luke Bryan, Lauren Alaina, Brothers Osborne, Dustin Lynch, Ella Langley, and Dan + Shay sharing holiday traditions, favorite foods, and personal stories. The barter-free special is available to country radio stations November nineteenth through twenty-ninth.
Premiere Networks will also offer a Smith Family Christmas Special beginning December eighteenth.

The Federal Communications Commission has issued sixty thousand dollars in fines against three pirate radio operators in New York and Massachusetts. Each operator faces a twenty-thousand-dollar penalty. In Brooklyn, Henderson Lennox Elcock was fined for operating Wild FM on 106.3. In Spring Valley, New York, Etzer Toussaint was fined for operating Radio Telemodel on 88.9. And in Hyannis, Massachusetts, Shane Kelly was fined for operating a station called The Test on 87.9. Kelly requested leniency after shutting down his station, but the FCC upheld the penalty. The commission says unauthorized stations can interfere with licensed broadcasters and emergency alert transmissions. All three operators have thirty days to pay their fines.

Television viewing declined 4.4 percent in August, according to Nielsen's latest report, as World Cup coverage ended and students headed back to school. Streaming continued to dominate, accounting for nearly half of all television viewing. YouTube reached a record 15.8 percent share, helped by increased viewing among adults 50 and older. Disney reclaimed second place among media distributors, while Netflix moved into third. Broadcast viewing dropped 14 percent, with ABC World News Tonight leading broadcast programs. Meanwhile, cable gained audience share as college football returned, with ESPN's North Carolina–TCU matchup topping cable telecasts. Nielsen also announced upcoming measurement changes, with September and October reports scheduled for release together later this year.

New York Public Radio has named Kimberly Watson its new Chief Development Officer. Watson will oversee fundraising, donor relations and membership growth for the organization, which operates WNYC, WQXR and WNYC Studios. She brings more than 30 years of experience working with major cultural institutions, including the Philadelphia Museum of Art and Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater. Her appointment comes as New York Public Radio expands its live events, digital initiatives and community engagement programs.

The Country Music Association, Belmont University, Disney, and the Nashville Convention and Visitors Corporation have announced a combined one-million-dollar donation to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library. The gift follows a star-studded television tribute featuring Carrie Underwood, Reba McEntire, Lainey Wilson, Vince Gill, and other country stars. Parton founded the Imagination Library in 1995 to provide free books to young children. The program has now distributed more than 300 million books worldwide. The tribute special, *I Will Always Love You: A Celebration of Dolly Parton*, is streaming on Disney Plus and Hulu.

Triton Digital's September podcast rankings are out, and iHeart Audience Network continues to dominate, generating more than 67 million average weekly downloads. Audioboom ranked second with 15.5 million, followed by Cumulus Podcast Network, BBC and Salem Podcast Network. Among individual podcasts, *Stuff You Should Know* claimed the top spot, followed by *Pod Save America*, *My Favorite Murder*, *The Dan Bongino Show* and *The Bulwark Podcast*. The rankings measure downloads among participating publishers using industry-certified standards.

Blackmagic Design has released two software updates for broadcast and video production equipment. Camera version 10.3.2 improves network control, switching between IP video and RAW workflows, and LUT functionality for the URSA Cine 12K LF. Converter Utility 12.4.1 delivers improvements and bug fixes for the company's 2110 IP Presentation Converter. Both updates are available through Blackmagic Design's support website.

Flor Leibaschoff has been named Chief Judge of the Radio Mercury Awards, which recognize excellence in radio and audio advertising. She's the Co-Founder and Chief Creative Officer of BeautifulBeast, with more than 25 years of industry experience. Leibaschoff made history as the first Hispanic female Chief Creative Officer in the United States. Her award-winning work has been recognized internationally, including at Cannes Lions and the Radio Mercury Awards. She calls the opportunity to lead judging for the 36-year-old competition a true honor.

Apple has announced the first fully authorized Fleetwood Mac documentary, titled Fleetwood Mac: The Chain, premiering January 29th, 2027, on Apple TV. Directed by Frank Marshall, the film features interviews, rare footage and personal stories from the legendary band. The release celebrates the 50th anniversary of Rumours, one of rock music's most iconic albums.

Momentum in sales doesn't happen by accident. It's built by stacking wins early in the week. In his latest blog, "Stack Wins Early in the Week," Chris Fleming of CD Media Consulting explains why scheduling important presentations, asking for decisions, and closing deals early can build confidence, strengthen customer relationships, and drive better results. His message is simple: stop waiting for momentum and start creating it. Read the full blog at Media Jobs Report dot com.

CBS is celebrating a strong premiere week, with multiplatform viewership climbing 14 percent over last year. The network averaged 8.6 million viewers and placed seven shows among the top 10 across broadcast and streaming. *Marshals* led with more than 15 million viewers, followed by *Tracker* and *60 Minutes*. Six CBS series topped 10 million viewers.

NPR is moving its public editor position to the University of Maryland's Philip Merrill College of Journalism beginning in January 2027. The multiyear partnership ends NPR's nearly seven-year arrangement with the Poynter Institute, where Kelly McBride has served as public editor since 2020. The incoming public editor will also serve as a visiting professor, focusing on journalism ethics, transparency and public trust. The university plans to begin accepting applications soon.

JJ Watt is officially CBS Sports' lead NFL game analyst under a new multi-year agreement. The three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year will continue alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson, including CBS's coverage of Super Bowl 62 in Atlanta. Watt joined CBS in 2023 as a studio analyst, moved into the broadcast booth in 2025, and joined the network's top announcing team this season.

Spotify and Harry Styles are teaming up for a Halloween dance party in New York City on October 31. The event, called Harryween, coincides with the final night of Styles' 30-show Madison Square Garden residency. Featuring the legendary Despacio sound system, the party runs from 6 to 9:30 p.m. Styles won't attend, but fans can RSVP through DICE. Admission is first-come, first-served.

Edison Research has released its Top 50 U.S. Podcasts for the third quarter of 2026, and the top five remain unchanged. The Joe Rogan Experience holds the number one spot, followed by Crime Junkie at number two, The Daily at number three, Call Her Daddy at number four, and SmartLess rounding out the top five. The rankings measure audience reach among weekly podcast listeners ages 13 and older. See the complete Top 50 rankings at Media Jobs Report dot com.

TEGNA is bringing Houston Comets basketball back to local television. Beginning with the 2027 WNBA season, games will air free on KTBU Channel 55, with select matchups also appearing on KHOU 11. The multi-year agreement includes streaming coverage and year-round team content. The Comets won the WNBA's first four championships before leaving the league in 2008.

FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez is urging broadcasters to resist political intimidation ahead of the midterm elections. In a letter to the National Association of Broadcasters, Gomez warned that airing polling results the Trump administration dislikes does not justify an FCC investigation. She emphasized that broadcasters must protect their editorial independence and should never have to choose between their licenses and their integrity.

Mentoring and Inspiring Women in Radio has selected Callie Luttman, morning host at Saga Communications' Mix 94.5 in Champaign-Urbana, as its 2026 Behind the Mic mentee. The year-long program provides leadership coaching and industry mentorship, along with an opportunity to attend the 2027 NAB Show in Las Vegas.

The ninth annual Canadian Podcast Awards are accepting nominations through November fourteenth. Canadian podcast professionals can nominate eligible shows across thirty-one categories, with winners selected by industry members. Public voting is also available through the People's Choice category. Winners will be announced December sixteenth.

Warner Music Group is combining its recorded music and publishing synchronization operations into one global division, promoting industry veteran Ron Broitman to President of Global Sync. The restructuring will simplify music licensing, speed up approvals and expand opportunities for artists and songwriters. Broitman will oversee worldwide sync operations across Warner's labels and publishing divisions.

Benztown is spreading holiday cheer with its free Christmas AudioPack, featuring 50 festive audio elements for radio stations of every format. From holiday sound effects to seasonal production elements, it's everything stations need to get into the Christmas spirit. Get the free pack at Benztown dot com slash Christmas.

Warner Music Group has promoted Roberto Andrade Dirak to President of Warner Music Latina and A&R for Latin America. Based in Miami, Andrade will expand his oversight of artist development, signings, and regional strategy. He has led Warner Music Latina for five years, helping develop rising Latin talent and strengthen the label's international presence.

Telemundo Las Vegas has added two journalists to its news team. Samanta Rodríguez joins as meteorologist after more than five years at Telemundo 39 in Dallas-Fort Worth. Ana Sofía Román joins as multimedia journalist from CoastTV News and Telemundo Delmarva. The 2026 Capital Emmy winner brings experience covering immigration, housing and local government. Both debuted October 26 on Noticiero Telemundo Las Vegas.

Audacy picked up five honors at the 2026 Buffalo Broadcasters Awards. WGR Sports Radio 550 was named Station of the Year, while WBEN's "A New Morning" won Radio Program of the Year. Sal Capaccio earned Sports Professional of the Year, his "It's Always Gameday in Buffalo" podcast won Podcast of the Year, and Owen Parker was named Breakout Talent of the Year.

TEGNA has named veteran television executive Mellynda Hartel president and general manager of three Florida stations. She'll oversee First Coast News in Jacksonville and CBS affiliate WTSP in Tampa. Hartel brings more than 30 years of experience and most recently led FOX stations KTVU and KICU in San Francisco.

The FCC has cited four Billings, Montana, radio stations for Emergency Alert System violations. Stations KEWF, KRPM, KYSX and KRSQ were flagged for monitoring an unauthorized EAS source, incomplete testing records and inadequate chief operator oversight. Licensee BMG Billings has 20 days to respond. Additional enforcement action remains possible.

Gray Media has named Jennifer Rieffer General Manager of CBS affiliate WBTV in Charlotte, effective November 16. Rieffer previously worked at WXIX FOX19 in Cincinnati, where she helped establish broadcasting partnerships with the Bengals and Reds. Her career also includes leadership positions in Flint, Michigan, and 24 years in Lexington, Kentucky.

Pierre Bouvard, Chief Insights Officer of the Cumulus Media Westwood One Audio Active Group, has published a new blog challenging eight common misconceptions about AM/FM radio. The research reveals that radio reaches 86 percent of Americans weekly, more than double what advertisers believe, and attracts over 63 million listeners ages 18 to 34. The findings also highlight radio's strong advertising returns, audience reach, and dominance in vehicles. Read the full story and Bouvard's blog at Media Jobs Report dot com.

New research from the Missouri School of Journalism is calling for better mental health support for reporters covering traumatic events. Researchers studying journalists who covered the Uvalde school shooting and the war in Ukraine found significant gaps in newsroom support. The studies suggest that empathy, better preparation and stronger mental health resources could help journalists cope with difficult assignments.

The National Religious Broadcasters has announced its 2027 Special Service and Media Award recipients. Honorees include Dr. Michael Youssef, WMCA Radio, CBN News and Moody Radio, with awards recognizing excellence in radio, television, digital media and Christian communications. Winners will be honored February 23 during the NRB International Christian Media Convention near Washington, D.C.

Hubbard Radio’s X102.3 is celebrating 25 years on the air in South Florida. The R&B station launched in October 2001 and has become a familiar voice across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast. West Palm Beach marked the milestone by proclaiming October 23 X102.3 Day and hosting a free waterfront celebration for listeners.

The Broadcasters Foundation of America is expanding financial assistance for radio and television professionals. Its new Extended Hardship Grants help broadcasters facing reduced income, family care expenses, housing emergencies and other unexpected hardships. The program joins the Foundation's existing monthly and emergency grants. Applications are now being accepted at broadcasters foundation dot org.

Edison Research at SSRS says AM/FM radio remains the leading source of in-car audio, including among people whose primary vehicle is electric. 
In the latest Weekly Insights, the company compared in-car listening among Americans age 13 and older with listening among EV drivers and riders. AM/FM accounted for 53 percent of in-car audio time among the overall population, compared with 42 percent among the EV group. Streaming music accounted for 17 percent of listening time overall and 22 percent among EV drivers and riders. The EV audience’s share of in-car listening time spent with podcasts was twice that of the overall population. SiriusXM also had a larger share among the EV group: 20 percent, compared with 16 percent overall.

Four major media and technology companies have announced November earnings dates. Qualcomm reports November fourth, followed by iHeartMedia and Skydance on November ninth. Warner Music Group reports November nineteenth. Investors can participate through scheduled conference calls or live webcasts. Find the complete schedule, telephone numbers, access codes and webcast links at Media Jobs Report dot com.

Westwood One and Silverloch are teaming up for special Election Day coverage on November third. Dan Bongino, Vince Coglianese, Hayley Caronia and Shawn Farash will deliver updates and commentary across radio, podcasts and streaming. Bongino wraps up the night with a live Rumble special beginning at eight Eastern. For affiliate sales inquiries, contact Susan Stephens, Senior Vice President & General Manager at Westwood One.

National Basketball Insider Brandon “Scoop B” Robinson is launching a new digital media network in early 2027. The platform will feature five original video and audio programs covering basketball, women's sports, hip-hop, fashion and lifestyle. Crossover Media Group will handle advertising sales, sponsorships and distribution. The venture also plans to hire professionals in video production, broadcasting and digital journalism.

TEGNA has named Brian Gregory President and General Manager of WCNC in Charlotte and WFMY in Greensboro. Gregory brings nearly 30 years of broadcasting experience and most recently led WVEC in Norfolk, where he expanded local streaming programming. He succeeds Joan Barrett, who was promoted to a regional leadership role.

The Academy of Country Music has announced its 2026-2027 Board of Directors and officers. Jeff Krones of CAA will serve as Chair, Becky Gardenhire of WME as President, and Rusty Gaston of Sony Publishing as Vice President. The Board includes 19 newly elected directors and 12 new directors-at-large, with representatives from Audacy, Cumulus, iHeart Country, Spotify and Apple Music.

What does it take to build a winning radio station? Brian Wright of Wright Media Group says success starts with three fundamentals: strategy, tactics, and execution. Strong leadership, clear priorities, and consistent follow-through turn good plans into lasting success. Read Wright's full blog at Media Jobs Report dot com.

New research from Northwestern University's Medill Local News Initiative finds Americans increasingly skeptical of the news media ahead of the midterm elections. Only 32 percent have high confidence in accurate election reporting, while sharp partisan divisions persist over journalists' intentions. Local news outlets remain among the most trusted sources. Read more at Media Jobs Report.

Audacy’s 106.5 The Wolf in Kansas City is adding Mo and StyckMan to its weekday lineup. Their show will air from 3 to 7 p.m. Central Time starting November 2. The award-winning duo also hosts shows in Chattanooga, Richmond and Memphis, along with Audacy’s nationwide overnight program, “3rd Shift Country.”

Peacock's new horror series Crystal Lake is off to a strong start. The Friday the 13th prequel generated 1.3 billion viewing minutes in its first 11 days, becoming Peacock's fourth-biggest scripted original debut. Starring Linda Cardellini, the eight-episode series is now streaming exclusively on Peacock.

The Missouri School of Journalism has named Amy Simons its next Associate Dean for Undergraduate Studies and Administration, effective May first. Simons, a professor and longtime faculty leader, succeeds Lynda Kraxberger, who is retiring after more than 35 years with the School. Simons will oversee undergraduate programs and student success initiatives.

On Air Fest is celebrating its 10th anniversary February 23rd through 25th in Brooklyn. The first-wave lineup includes Megan Rapinoe, Dr. Sanjay Gupta, Audie Cornish, Ari Shapiro and Dan Harris. The festival also features Bloomberg's Podcast Business Summit and the Ambies Awards, celebrating excellence in podcasting. Tickets are available now, with additional programming to be announced.

SiriusXM is getting into the holiday spirit with 25 seasonal music channels beginning November second. The lineup includes Christmas classics, country, rock, jazz and soul, plus specialty channels featuring Jimmy Fallon, Hallmark, Smokey Robinson and Trans-Siberian Orchestra. Many channels will be available on the SiriusXM app and satellite radio throughout the holidays.

NPR has named David Berzin Senior Vice President of Product and Data. Berzin joins from Hearst Magazines, where he led international product development and artificial intelligence initiatives. He previously held digital leadership roles at Viacom and MTV. At NPR, Berzin will oversee digital products, audience engagement and data strategy, helping strengthen connections with listeners and member stations while supporting new revenue opportunities.
